# Copilot Instructions
## Project Guidelines
- **Number one priority for all pages:** build and verify in `Table/API/UI` order. Confirm the database table/schema first, then align API/backend contracts and persistence, then implement or update the UI.
- Use the naming convention `ApiClients.CrmConfiguration*.cs` for CRM Configuration ApiClient sealed partial class files.
- Use existing `enterprise.css` styles for UI; do not add workflow functionality unless explicitly requested. For UI fixes in this codebase, prefer native Blazor markup plus scoped Razor CSS so CSS isolation applies correctly. For app-wide Blazor visual/theme fixes, use the global CSS layer instead of CSS-isolation ::deep overrides in layout/component scoped CSS. When removing or altering stylesheet rules or other UI dependencies, scope those removals/changes to the specific page requested; do not modify or remove global styles or shared UI dependencies unless the user explicitly requests a global change.
- Do not use third-party grid/dialog/toast CSS frameworks in this repository; use native Blazor components, custom AMS components, and existing `enterprise.css` patterns instead.
- Scope stylesheet or UI dependency removals to the specific page requested unless the user explicitly asks for a global change.
- All pages must use the full available content width by default. Avoid narrow fixed-width page shells, centered max-width containers, or layouts that leave unused horizontal space; align page margins and responsive behavior with the enterprise full-width Submission and Submission Detail patterns unless the user explicitly requests a constrained layout.
- Before creating DTO, check DB first if already exists; if yes, make DB the source of truth. If not, create a new DTO and add it to the DB. Always add the base fields to the DTO, and if any new fields are added, make sure to add them to the DB as well.
- **DB is always the source of truth.** When there is a mismatch between code (DTOs, repositories, requests) and the actual database schema, update the C# code to match the DB — never alter the DB to match the code unless explicitly instructed.
- When reviewing or modifying the AMS data model, verify that entity tables, foreign-key relationships, indexes, application workflows, and seed data remain mutually consistent, with no missing relationship gaps.
- When writing Dapper SQL for tables that have no `IsDeleted` column, pass `hasSoftDelete: false` to `RepositorySql.BuildPagedSearchSql`.
- Always add validations to the DTOs and requests, and ensure that the validations are consistent with the database constraints. If a field is required in the database, it should be marked as required in the DTO/request as well.
- Always add `[Required]`, `[StringLength]`, and `[Range]` data annotation attributes to all form model classes in Blazor pages that have user entry, matching the constraints of the corresponding request record and DB column. Always add `<ValidationMessage For="() => _form.Field" class="text-danger" />` after every input in dialogs/forms, including dropdowns. All Blazor `<ValidationMessage>` components in this repository must include `class="text-danger"` so validation messages render in red like CRM Configuration pages. Do not add `<ValidationMessage>` without `class="text-danger"`.
- **Do not add required validation messages in UI forms; avoid adding ValidationMessage elements specifically for required-field validation unless explicitly requested.**
- Always add error handling on data load (`LoadAsync`/`OnInitializedAsync`): store the exception message in a `string? _loadError` field and display it as a Bootstrap `alert-danger` div below the filter panel. All `catch` blocks in `SaveAsync`, `ExecuteDeleteAsync`, and update methods must include `ex.Message` in the toast content (e.g., `$"Save failed: {ex.Message}"`). Never use empty `catch { }` blocks.
- **Professional modal pattern**: All create/edit dialogs must use the native enterprise modal structure. Place a `<div class="um-modal-header">` containing a contextual Bootstrap icon (`<i class="bi bi-*">`), a `<span>` with the dialog title, and a ghost close button (`<button type="button" class="um-btn um-btn-ghost um-btn-sm ms-auto" @onclick="() => _showForm = false"><i class="bi bi-x-lg"></i></button>`) as the first child inside the modal. Wrap all form fields in `<div class="um-modal-body"><div class="um-form-grid">...</div></div>`. Use `<div class="um-modal-footer">` for action buttons. Delete confirm dialogs keep the `um-confirm-dialog` structure unchanged.
- **Validation and error messages styling**: All client-side validation messages (`<ValidationMessage>`) in all Blazor pages must render in red exactly like CRM Configuration pages by using `class="text-danger"` on every inline validation message, without exception. Do not add a `<ValidationMessage>` without `class="text-danger"`. For `alert-danger` banners, also add the inline style `style="border-left: 4px solid #dc3545; animation: um-shake 0.3s ease;"` and include the keyframe `@keyframes um-shake { 0%,100%{transform:translateX(0)} 25%{transform:translateX(-4px)} 75%{transform:translateX(4px)} }` in the page's scoped CSS or `enterprise.css` if not already present. Toast error messages must use enterprise toast classes and include `ex.Message` in the content.
- **Clickable grid rows**: All enterprise grids must support row selection using the native `AppGrid`/`GridEvents` pattern or an equivalent table row click handler. Add a `void OnRowSelected(RowSelectEventArgs<T> args) => OpenEdit(args.Data);` handler in `@code` when using `AppGrid`. Action buttons (edit/delete) inside row templates must use `@onclick:stopPropagation="true"` to prevent the row-click from firing when the user clicks those buttons.
- All delete or remove actions must always show a confirmation dialog before executing. Never execute delete, remove, revoke, deactivate-as-delete, or role-removal actions directly from a button click without first asking the user to confirm.
- **Clickable KPI filters**: All KPI cards/tiles on list, dashboard, and configuration pages must dynamically filter the displayed data when clicked. Use active filter state (for example `_activeFilter` / `_kpiFilter`), bind grids/lists to the filtered collection, apply filters immediately on click, and visually mark the active KPI card.
- **Search/Filter Panel Layout**: For search/filter panel layouts in this AMS Blazor codebase, make the search box longer than the filter controls by default. For the CRM Pricing Rules page search row, reuse the visual and responsive CSS pattern from `/crm/pricing/classes` rather than maintaining custom search-row styling.
- **Base fields for new tables**: All new tables added to the database must include all base fields: `TenantId`, `CreatedDateUtc`, `CreatedByUserId`, `ModifiedDateUtc`, `ModifiedByUserId`, `IsDeleted`. When creating new database tables in this repository, always include the standard base/audit fields.
- For this AMS Blazor codebase, do not use mock or hardcoded UI data for selectable values, statuses, options, settings, or configuration lists. All selectable/configuration data must be database-backed and loaded through the backend/API. When new values are needed, create or update the appropriate table and seed data instead of hardcoding values in C#, Razor, JavaScript, or CSS. Keep database seed/configuration data, DTOs, requests, repositories, API clients, and Blazor UI models synchronized so the database remains the source of truth across the full Table/API/UI flow. Check existing app modules first to avoid duplicating functionality.
- For fields with multiple predefined values, use dropdown lists rather than textboxes in Blazor forms.
- For certificate View Policy navigation, treat `/policies/{guid}` as a route format and use the selected certificate's dynamic PolicyId rather than hardcoding a specific policy GUID.
- Use `DMS.DocumentKind` and `DMS.DocumentGroup` for normalized document management tables. For document configuration/category work, use `DMS.DocumentGroup` as the canonical runtime table instead of `Documents.DocumentConfigItem`. For document category normalization, ensure that `Master.Category` contains category/grouping values, while `DMS.DocumentGroup` contains document group/config item values; do not interchange these mappings.
- When making light-mode text color/style overrides, ensure selectors do not affect or compromise dark theme behavior.
- For AMS search boxes, light mode glow can stay subtle, but dark mode search boxes should be made noticeably visible using a brighter blue-tinted surface, border, glow, icon, and placeholder styling.
- When polishing UI in dark mode, fix white/light backgrounds and contrast/readability issues, not just decorative styling.
- **When fixing UI/CSS issues, prefer removing the source CSS/markup that causes the problem instead of adding compensating overrides; if a style is not working because of overlap, remove the conflicting old CSS first.** User strongly prefers removal-based fixes over adding overrides; avoid using stronger CSS overrides like !important to compensate for conflicts, and remove/narrow conflicting CSS at the source instead.
- Implement enterprise features using database-backed data only: no mock or hardcoded operational data; add or update tables and configuration/reference seeds as needed; synchronize all existing data into the authoritative model.
- When adding platform pages or related workflows, also add discoverable navigation entries in NavSidebar under the correct functional section, including relevant portal and hub-center links.
- **Enterprise-facing pages should be polished and support both light and dark application themes.** Keep headers compact and ensure all text has strong contrast in the light theme.
- In light theme, secondary buttons placed on pale or gradient headers must use dark text and a visibly contrasting border/background rather than white text.

## CRMConfiguration Guidelines
- CRM Configuration pages are Blazor pages under `TenantConfig/CrmConfig` and should follow the established CRM Configuration page pattern used by Lead Sources, Lead Statuses, Opportunity Stages, Duplicate Rules, Assignment Rules, and CRM Custom Fields. Preserve existing functionality and add or polish features without removing them, following the `/crm/opportunities` layout pattern.
- Use `enterprise.css` design-system classes for CRM Configuration UI. Do not add one-off page styles unless the class is reusable and belongs in `enterprise.css`. When removing or altering stylesheet rules or UI dependencies for CRM Configuration pages, scope changes to the specific page requested and avoid global removals unless explicitly requested.
- Keep the database as the source of truth for CRM Configuration schema, DTOs, requests, repositories, and form models. Update C# code to match the DB schema when mismatches are found.
- CRM Configuration DTOs, requests, and Blazor form models must include validation consistent with database constraints. Required DB fields must be required in requests and form models.
- Add `[Required]`, `[StringLength]`, and `[Range]` attributes to CRM Configuration form model properties where applicable. Every input, dropdown, checkbox, and textarea used for user entry must have a matching `<ValidationMessage For="() => _form.Field" class="text-danger" />` when validation applies.
- CRM Configuration pages must use `AppPageHeader` with a contextual Bootstrap icon, title, subtitle, primary add button, and refresh button.
- CRM Configuration pages must include KPI cards in a `pc-kpi-strip`. KPI cards should be clickable filters using `_activeFilter`, `_filtered`, `SetFilter(...)`, and `ApplyFilter()`. The active KPI card must use `pc-kpi-card--active` and each KPI card should include a descriptive `title` tooltip.
- CRM Configuration grids must bind to `_filtered`, not directly to `_items`, so KPI filters and search results stay consistent.
- CRM Configuration `AppGrid` rows must be clickable to edit. Add `<GridEvents TValue="T" RowSelected="OnRowSelected" />` inside the grid and implement `void OnRowSelected(RowSelectEventArgs<T> args) => OpenEdit(args.Data);`.
- Grid edit/delete buttons must include `@onclick:stopPropagation="true"` so button clicks do not also trigger the row-click edit behavior.
- Add clickable-row affordance through `enterprise.css` using enterprise grid/table classes, not page-specific CSS.
- Create/edit CRM Configuration modals must use the professional native enterprise modal pattern with a custom `<div class="um-modal-header">` as the first child inside the modal.
- CRM Configuration modal headers must include a contextual Bootstrap icon, a title span that switches between add/edit text, and a ghost close button using `um-btn um-btn-ghost um-btn-sm ms-auto` with the `bi-x-lg` icon.
- CRM Configuration modal form fields must be wrapped in `<div class="um-modal-body"><div class="um-form-grid">...</div></div>`.
- CRM Configuration modal action buttons must use `<div class="um-modal-footer">`; do not use `um-dialog-footer` in create/edit dialogs.
- CRM Configuration delete confirmation dialogs must keep the professional `um-confirm-dialog` structure with a contextual danger icon (`um-confirm-icon um-confirm-icon--danger`), clear confirmation text, and `um-modal-footer` actions.
- CRM Configuration pages must include load error handling. `LoadAsync` / `OnInitializedAsync` should store exception text in `string? _loadError` and display a Bootstrap `alert-danger` message below the filter panel.
- CRM Configuration save, delete, and update catch blocks must include `ex.Message` in toast content and use enterprise danger toast styling for errors. Do not use empty catch blocks.
- CRM Configuration success toasts should use enterprise success toast styling and should reload data after successful create/update/delete.
- CRM Configuration navigation entries belong under the `CRM Configuration` section in `NavSidebar.razor` with contextual Bootstrap icons and `/tenant/crm/...` routes.
- For Producer and CSR pages, retrieve the user list and filter by the user's Role field to get Producer and CSR lists.
- For `/workbench/producer`, the page is intentionally viewed and used as the Tenant Admin User; workbench data should remain scoped to the Tenant Admin User while avoiding mock/default/computed data.
- For CRM Leads detail actions, place Edit, Assign, and Disqualify in a single row above a full-width Convert button. Render the Convert button as full-width below the action row and center its content.
- For CRM Lead detail document uploads, reuse `EnterpriseDocumentUpload` and default Document Type to `Lead`, Category to `CRM`, and Tags to `Lead` (singular).
- For Blazor popups/forms in this repository, remove required field validation message components when requested; avoid showing required validation messages in the Document Group popup.
- On CRM Lead detail pages, document uploads should reuse the Policy Upload Document component/pattern and default the Tags field to `Leads`.

## AMS CRM Workflow Hierarchy
- The AMS CRM workflow hierarchy should be Lead (unqualified) → Account (organization/person master record) → Opportunity (revenue potential) → Submission (underwriting package) → SubmissionMarket → QuoteRequest → Quote → CustomerAuthorization/Proposal → BindRequest → Policy.
- Cardinality: 1 Lead maps to 0 or 1 Account, 1 Account has many Opportunities, 1 Opportunity has many Submissions, 1 Submission has many SubmissionMarkets and QuoteRequests, 1 QuoteRequest can produce 0 or more Quotes, and Policy is created only after confirmed binding.

## AMS Enterprise Submission, Market, Quote, Binding, and Policy Workflow
- Model `Submit to Market` and `Request Quote` as related but distinct enterprise capabilities. `Submit to Market` tracks distribution of a submission package to carriers, wholesalers, MGAs, brokers, or underwriters. `Request Quote` tracks the request for pricing and coverage terms from a specific market.
- Implement this workflow in `Table/API/UI` order. Confirm or create the database tables, status/configuration seed data, audit fields, and relationships first; then align repositories/services/API contracts; then update Blazor UI actions and screens.
- Workflow statuses, delivery methods, confirmation sources, authorization methods, decline reasons, and other selectable workflow values must be database-backed configuration/seed data. Do not hardcode these values in pages, DTOs, request handlers, repositories, or API clients.
- When adding workflow status/configuration values, keep seed data, lookup/configuration tables, DTOs, validation rules, API clients, and UI dropdowns synchronized. The UI should load available values through backend/API data, not local arrays.
- Keep `SubmissionMarket` and `QuoteRequest` as separate business objects when implementing enterprise placement workflows. A market can exist without a quote request, and a quote request can exist without a quote.
- `SubmissionMarket` owns distribution metadata such as submission, market/carrier, submitted date, delivery status, sent by, received/viewed dates, underwriter, and notes.
- `QuoteRequest` owns pricing-request metadata such as submission market, requested market, products or lines, coverage option, requested effective date, requested date/time, requested by, submission version, delivery method, assigned underwriter, response due date, retry count, correlation/external reference IDs, carrier reference number, response date, status, and error details.
- All new workflow tables must include the standard base/audit fields required by this repository: `TenantId`, `CreatedDateUtc`, `CreatedByUserId`, `ModifiedDateUtc`, `ModifiedByUserId`, and `IsDeleted`.
- Preserve tenant isolation in every workflow query and mutation. Quote, bind, policy, market, authorization, proposal, document, activity, task, billing, and commission records must remain scoped to the correct tenant and related parent records.
- A producer clicking `Request Quote` must create a `QuoteRequest` record first, before contacting a carrier, MGA, wholesaler, portal, rater, or manual underwriter workflow. Do not create an empty `Quote` at request time.
- A `Quote` represents an actual pricing and coverage offer returned by the market. Create a `Quote` only when the market response includes quote/pricing data. Declines, referrals, failures, and requests for more information update the `QuoteRequest`; they must not create a `Quote`.
- Preserve this lifecycle even for immediate API rating: create `QuoteRequest` → send carrier/rater request → receive response → create `Quote` only if pricing is returned.
- Support both workflow models: personal-lines/API carriers may expose a single `Request Quote` user action that internally creates `SubmissionMarket`, creates `QuoteRequest`, calls the API, and creates `Quote` only on quote response; commercial-lines/manual markets should allow `Submit to Market` first, then `Request Quote` when underwriting requirements are satisfied.
- Delivery method should drive workflow behavior. API/rater requests can dispatch automatically; email-based markets should generate/send request packages; portal/manual markets should create placement tasks and allow users to record external carrier reference numbers and responses.
- Use event-driven/background processing for carrier communication where applicable: UI creates `QuoteRequest`, publishes or enqueues quote-request work, a background worker/carrier connector dispatches the request, and the system updates `QuoteRequest` to submitted, acknowledged, under review, quoted, declined, or more information required.
- Submission status is independent from child `QuoteRequest`, `Quote`, `Proposal`, `BindRequest`, and `Policy` statuses. Submission status should summarize the overall workflow, not replace child record statuses.
- Prefer deriving or synchronizing submission-level status from child records to avoid drift. Examples: no quote requests means ready for marketing; active quote requests and no quotes means marketing; at least one quote means quotes received; proposal created means proposal prepared; customer authorization/selected quote means customer accepted; bind in progress means binding; policy exists after confirmed bind means bound.
- Status transitions should be enforced in backend application services, not only in Blazor UI. UI buttons should call backend actions that validate the current state, required child records, tenant scope, and authorization before changing workflow state.
- Record audit/history entries for material workflow transitions, including quote request creation/dispatch, carrier acknowledgments, quote received, decline, more information required, quote approval/presentation, customer authorization, bind request submission, carrier confirmation, and policy creation.
- Recommended submission statuses: `Draft`, `In Progress`, `Ready for Marketing`, `Marketing`, `Quotes Requested`, `Quotes Received`, `Proposal Prepared`, `Presented`, `Customer Accepted`, `Binding`, `Bound`, `Lost`, `Cancelled`, `Closed`.
- Recommended quote-request statuses: `Draft`, `Validation Required`, `Pending Dispatch`, `Submitted`, `Acknowledged`, `Under Review`, `More Information Required`, `Referred`, `Quoted`, `Declined`, `Withdrawn`, `Expired`, `Cancelled`, `Failed`.
- Recommended quote statuses: `Received`, `Under Review`, `Revision Requested`, `Approved for Presentation`, `Presented`, `Selected`, `Not Selected`, `Rejected`, `Expired`, `Superseded`, `Bound`.
- Treat the recommended status lists as seed/configuration data definitions, not as hardcoded enum-only UI logic. If enums are used in C# for safety, they must be mapped to and synchronized with the database-backed status/configuration records.
- Before dispatching a quote request, validate quote readiness: applicant/account, line of business, effective date, risk details, requested coverages/limits, underwriting questions, required documents, selected market, producer, and branch information. Missing required items should set or return `Validation Required` with actionable missing-item details.
- When a market requests additional information, update the `QuoteRequest` to `More Information Required`, create an underwriting requirement/task, notify responsible users, and allow resubmission without overwriting historical requests or responses.
- When a market declines, capture decline reason, decline category, date, underwriter comments, and remarketing recommendation when applicable. Do not create a quote for declines.
- Support multiple quote requests and revisions per submission/market. Re-quoting because of changed limits, coverage options, or customer changes should create a new `QuoteRequest` and, if pricing is returned, a new `Quote`, preserving the full audit trail.
- Enable quote comparison when one or more usable quotes exist. A quote should be comparable whether it was returned by API, entered manually, received by email, or imported from a carrier portal.
- Treat `Proposal` as a presentation/sales artifact, not the source of truth for quote or policy data. A proposal may contain one or more quotes through a join object such as `ProposalQuote`, and a quote may appear in more than one proposal version.
- Proposal generation should be strongly encouraged for new business and multi-quote comparisons, but it is not mandatory for all binds. Do not make `ProposalId` mandatory on `BindRequest`.
- Require documented customer authorization before binding. Use a `CustomerAuthorization` business object to capture acceptance method such as signed proposal, email approval, recorded call, e-signature, portal acceptance, written instruction, carrier proposal, or manual acknowledgment.
- A bind workflow starts from a selected/accepted quote and customer authorization. Producer action should create a `BindRequest`, not a `Policy`.
- `BindRequest` owns binding metadata such as submission, quote, customer authorization, requested effective date/time, status, submitted at/by, confirmation source, carrier reference number, binder number, policy number, confirmed at, confirming carrier contact/user, final premium, down payment, outstanding subjectivities, confirmation notes, confirmation document, integration correlation ID, and external transaction ID.
- Recommended bind-request statuses: `Draft`, `Pending Validation`, `Pending Authorization`, `Pending Payment`, `Ready To Submit`, `Submitted`, `Acknowledged`, `Carrier Reviewing`, `More Information Required`, `Conditionally Approved`, `Verbally Confirmed`, `Confirmed`, `Bound`, `Declined`, `Withdrawn`, `Expired`, `Failed`.
- A successful bind-request transmission is not carrier confirmation. `Submitted` or HTTP success only means the request was received/accepted for processing; it does not mean coverage is bound.
- Carrier confirmation means authoritative evidence from the carrier, MGA, wholesaler, or authorized underwriter that coverage is accepted and placed in force. Supported confirmation sources should include API, webhook/polling, carrier portal, email, phone/verbal, binder document, and manual entry with supporting documentation.
- For verbal/phone confirmation, require stronger documentation such as underwriter name/company, date/time, agency user, call notes, follow-up written confirmation flag, and supporting evidence where agency rules require it.
- Create the AMS `Policy` record only after reliable carrier confirmation that coverage is bound. Do not create a policy when a quote is received or when the producer merely clicks bind/request bind.
- Distinguish the carrier-issued legal policy from the AgencyBinder internal AMS policy record: carrier generates official policy contract/documents, while AgencyBinder creates/maintains policy record, servicing lifecycle, and should use PendingIssue/Issued/Active style status semantics when applicable.
- Distinguish the carrier's legal policy contract from the AgencyBinder/AMS policy record. The carrier normally generates the official policy number, declarations, policy contract, forms, endorsements, billing schedule, and final policy documents. AgencyBinder creates and manages the internal policy record, policy term, coverage records, insured/risk links, premium/commission records, binder/policy document references, servicing workflows, renewal tracking, and audit trail.
- Policy creation should be owned by a dedicated policy service or handler after bind confirmation, not embedded directly in UI or binding code. Prefer flow: `BindConfirmedEvent` or `PolicyCreationRequested` → policy service creates policy, policy term, coverages, billing, commissions, documents, activities, renewal schedule, tasks, and audit records.
- Keep service boundaries clear: submission service manages submissions, submission markets, and quote requests; quote service manages returned quotes and quote review; binding service manages bind requests and carrier confirmation; policy service owns policy creation and servicing lifecycle after coverage is bound.
- Background workers that dispatch quote or bind requests must be idempotent and retry-safe. Use request IDs, external transaction IDs, correlation IDs, retry counts, and status checks to prevent duplicate carrier submissions, duplicate quotes, duplicate bind confirmations, or duplicate policies.
- Blazor UI should expose workflow actions based on backend-calculated eligibility, not duplicated client-side rules. Examples: enable `Request Quote` only when validation passes or missing items can be displayed; enable `Generate Proposal` only for usable approved quotes; enable `Request Bind` only when a selected quote and customer authorization exist; enable `Confirm Bind` only for submitted/acknowledged/reviewing bind requests.
- Never delete unsuccessful markets, declined quote requests, rejected quotes, or superseded revisions.
- Avoid repetitive process narration or output loops; keep implementation progress concise and proceed directly with validation.

## Shared Validation Rules
- Prefer shared/global validation rules and attributes instead of component-scoped validation implementations.

## Insurance Knowledge Center
- Implement the Insurance Knowledge Center inside the existing AgencyBinder solution as a bounded modular-monolith module: separate Knowledge Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Contracts projects, a separate knowledge SQL schema and migrations, explicit contracts, existing API/Web/Worker hosts, no direct cross-module table access, and no separate deployment initially.
- For the Insurance Knowledge Center, implement a SQL Server-backed Insurance Semantic Layer with no mock or hard-coded UI/application data. Create, seed, update, and synchronize database data as needed. Keep the AMS operational database and workflows authoritative; semantic features are optional/advisory initially and must fail without blocking core operations. Use deterministic approved concepts/mappings/rules, human approval for AI suggestions, tenant-aware security/audit/versioning, SKOS-style concepts and hierarchy, relational closure tables, and defer graph/RDF/OWL/SHACL projections until proven use cases require them.

## AgencyBinder Public Website Content
- For AgencyBinder public website content, give heavy prominence to the Intelligence Platform, explicit AI positioning, and Core Engines. Present workflows only as high-level concepts rather than detailed internal steps, and use the home index page as the primary showcase.

## Troubleshooting Guidelines
- When troubleshooting, provide direct instructions tied to the exact current log/state; avoid mixing alternative paths or unnecessary background details.

## POLOXI Wide Intelligence Pipeline
- In the POLOXI Wide intelligence pipeline (IntelligenceWideService), any new rules or fixes must never contradict or feed back into the computation of merit factors (composite scores, evidence coverage/confidence, EEA exclusive hosts, FD fragment domination, SB kind demotion, support counts). New logic must operate strictly downstream of factor computation — ranking, filtering, and disclosure only.
- **V3.10.1 Merit-Tier Final Ranking (mandatory stage in the POLOXI core end-to-end flow):** every POLOXI ranking path must apply this algorithm after factor computation and before returning results: (1) constraint violators and support-excluded candidates are removed from the final ranking entirely — they never occupy Top N slots or appear as 0% rows; (2) admitted candidates order by disclosed merit tier first (STRONG > MODERATE > LIMITED), then composite score, so SB kind demotion affects rank, not only disclosure; (3) tier/admission disclosures must never contradict — excluded candidates report `EXCLUDED` for both `SupportTierCode` and `AdmissionModeCode`, and dictionary-miss defaults must never overstate support (default to `EXCLUDED`, never `STRONG`/`NORMAL`). All exclusions are per-execution verdicts about evidence in context, never persistent blocklists — an entity excluded in one run must compete fresh in every new run.
- For POLOXI changes, preserve benchmark comparability: distinguish formula changes from factor-input attribution changes, explicitly report when a recall fix can change benchmark scores/rankings, and validate against the benchmark before accepting it.
